Firefighters Battle Petrol Car Blaze on Denshaw Grove Morley 2026

Last updated: September 29, 2026 10:57 am
News Desk
10:56 am
Newsroom Staff -
@theleedstimes
Share
Credit: Google Street View/yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk

Key Points

  • Multiple emergency 999 calls were made by residents after a petrol car burst into flames on Denshaw Grove, Morley.
  • Emergency services received the initial report at 9:59 pm on Friday, September 25.
  • One fire engine from West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service was dispatched immediately to the scene.
  • Upon arrival, firefighters found the vehicle fully engulfed in flames.
  • A firefighter wearing breathing apparatus utilized a hose reel to battle and extinguish the blaze.
  • Emergency crews successfully brought the incident under control and vacated the area shortly after 10:30 pm.

Morley (The Leeds Times) September 29, 2026 – Firefighters were called to tackle an late-night vehicle fire on Denshaw Grove, Morley, after multiple local residents placed emergency 999 calls when a petrol car became fully engulfed in flames.

  • What happened during the car fire on Denshaw Grove?
  • How did emergency services respond to the Morley vehicle blaze?

As reported by journalist Bill Hannam of the Yorkshire Evening Post, West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service (WYFRS) Control received the urgent calls at approximately 9:59 pm on Friday, September 25. One fire engine was dispatched to the street in Morley, where firefighters discovered the vehicle well alight.

According to an official incident report released by West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service, crews tackled the blaze using specialist protective gear and equipment. As stated in the official summary from West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service,

“1 fire engine was mobilised and found a petrol car well alight on arrival. Crews used 1 hose reel and 1 firefighter wore breathing apparatus to extinguish the fire”.

Emergency crews remained at the location on Denshaw Grove to ensure the area was safe and fully damp down the vehicle, leaving the scene shortly after 10:30 pm. No injuries or structural damage to surrounding properties were reported in connection with the incident.

What happened during the car fire on Denshaw Grove?

The incident unfolded late on Friday night when residents on Denshaw Grove in Morley observed flames emanating from a parked petrol vehicle. The sudden blaze prompted multiple immediate calls to Fire Control.

West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service responded swiftly by sending a single crew. Upon arrival, firefighters quickly established a safety perimeter around the burning vehicle. One firefighter, equipped with breathing apparatus to shield against toxic smoke and fumes, deployed a hose reel line to tackle the main body of the fire. The fire was successfully doused within half an hour, preventing potential spread to adjacent residential property or neighboring parked cars.

How did emergency services respond to the Morley vehicle blaze?

The response was managed through West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service’s central control room, which coordinated the deployment as soon as 999 calls were validated. Firefighters executed standard operating procedures for petrol vehicle fires, which involve deploying specialized hose reel jets and breathing gear to handle high temperatures and volatile fuel combustion. Crews remained on scene for approximately 30 minutes following suppression to verify that the vehicle was fully cooled and posed no further risk of re-ignition.

Background of the particular development

Vehicle fires present recurring operational challenges for urban and suburban fire services across West Yorkshire. Standard protocol for West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service involves rapid deployment of localized appliances to prevent thermal runoff and exposure hazards, particularly in residential developments like Denshaw Grove where vehicles are parked close to housing structures. Petrol-fueled vehicle fires present specific hazards due to fuel tank integrity, flammable fluids, and synthetic materials inside passenger cabins, requiring immediate suppression via high-pressure hose reels and breathing apparatus for personnel safety.

Prediction

This development primarily impacts local residents of Denshaw Grove and the broader Morley community. In the immediate term, residents may experience heightened awareness surrounding street parking safety and localized traffic disruptions during recovery operations. For West Yorkshire Fire and Rescue Service and local council authorities, incidents of this nature reinforce the ongoing demand for efficient emergency response times in suburban neighborhoods. Additionally, vehicle owners in the residential area are likely to remain vigilant regarding vehicle maintenance and security measures to minimize risk factors associated with sudden vehicular blazes.
